stage: synthetic end-to-end test of local round transport and round publication
status: passed: run 1 (full circuit), run 2 (proposer-verifier without a challenger) and run 3 (full-circuit regression)
model: claude-opus-5-5 (coordinator); test sessions claude-sonnet-5-5 at low effort
owner_instruction_2026_10_14: keep working until you can claim that the local run through proposer-challenger-verifier-proposer circuit can work effectively
design: Three fresh headless sessions of the pinned Claude Code 2.1.293 CLI on a throwaway fixture with no scientific content. The proposer used settings derived from runs/CLD-P05-LAUNCH-0001/launch-settings.json (sha256 6009cc41dd0d8f8c6714bb81227166d0490632b64a2d92221c790bb96a005cc9); the challenger and verifier used stand-in settings granting what config/round-transport.json requires of their platforms. Each session froze and transmitted with its own read-only copy of the tools, waited through a background command and acted only when the CLI woke it.

run2_no_challenger.note: Proposer and verifier sessions only, as while the GPT challenger is at its usage limit. The verifier woke on the proposer release, reviewed it directly and sent a verification delivery naming the reviewed release; the proposer woke on it. A first attempt crashed in the harness itself (a splice error duplicated main), before any check; it was fixed and rerun.

run3_full_regression.note: Full circuit after the verifier-only changes, consent checks and receipt-only waiting.

findings: The proposer received challenger material only inside the verified-challenge delivery that carried the verifier release.
Each session woke from its background wait without polling: the proposer once, the challenger and the verifier twice.
Receipt files acknowledged every delivery exactly once; no delivery was returned twice.
The publisher found exactly one completed round and built a validated round commit holding the proposer, challenger and verifier releases plus the round record.
network_incident: The first publication dry run failed at git fetch with a GitHub SSL_ERROR_SYSCALL from the host VPN. The same fixture was published again with circuit_test.py --publish-fixture after GitHub was reachable.
limits: The challenger and verifier stand-ins are Claude Code sessions. The real Codex challenger and DeepSeek verifier runtimes still need the same grants from their coordinators.

The dry run stops before git push and gh pr create. Synthetic sessions are deliberately unregistered, so only a real round can exercise the push; it uses the same git and gh path as this project's other PRs.
All sessions share one OS account; sandbox grants are the boundary, not adversarial isolation.
contamination_events: None. No role session, packet or private material was used.
independence_attestation: Coordinator infrastructure test only; no scientific content, verification or approval.
